E-waste.Preparation Steps: Remove all batteries and delete personal data before recycling.
E-waste.Disposal Warnings: Never throw in regular trash. Contains toxic heavy metals like lead and mercury.
E-waste.Environmental Impact: Proper recycling prevents soil and water contamination while recovering valuable metals.
E-waste.Recycling Process: Devices are shredded, and metals/plastics are separated using magnets and water currents.
E-waste.Interesting Facts: Only about 20% of global e-waste is formally recycled.
E-waste.Common Mistakes: Throwing small electronics like earbuds in the regular bin.

automobile wastes.Preparation Steps: Drain all fluids (oil, coolant) into sealed, leak-proof containers.
automobile wastes.Disposal Warnings: Highly flammable and toxic. Keep away from heat sources.
automobile wastes.Environmental Impact: One gallon of motor oil can contaminate one million gallons of water.
automobile wastes.Recycling Process: Oil is re-refined, tires are shredded for playground surfaces, and scrap metal is melted.
automobile wastes.Interesting Facts: Used motor oil never wears out, it just gets dirty and can be recycled infinitely.
automobile wastes.Common Mistakes: Pouring used oil down storm drains.

battery waste.Preparation Steps: Tape the terminals of lithium/button batteries with clear tape to prevent short circuits.
battery waste.Disposal Warnings: Lithium batteries can catch fire if crushed in garbage trucks. Do not puncture.
battery waste.Environmental Impact: Prevents toxic chemicals (lithium, cadmium, lead) from leaching into groundwater.
battery waste.Recycling Process: Batteries are sorted by chemistry, crushed, and metals are extracted via smelting.
battery waste.Interesting Facts: Lead-acid car batteries are the most recycled consumer product in the world.
battery waste.Common Mistakes: Tossing rechargeable batteries into the household recycling bin.

glass waste.Preparation Steps: Rinse lightly to remove food residue. Lids can usually remain on.
glass waste.Disposal Warnings: Broken glass should be wrapped in thick paper and labeled before disposal.
glass waste.Environmental Impact: Recycling glass reduces energy costs by 20-30% compared to making new glass.
glass waste.Recycling Process: Glass is crushed into cullet, sorted by color, melted, and molded into new products.
glass waste.Interesting Facts: Glass is 100% recyclable and can be recycled endlessly without loss of quality.
glass waste.Common Mistakes: Mixing Pyrex, mirrors, or window glass with bottle glass (they have different melting points).

light bulbs.Preparation Steps: Wrap securely to prevent breakage during transport.
light bulbs.Disposal Warnings: CFLs and fluorescent tubes contain toxic mercury vapor. Clean up immediately if broken.
light bulbs.Environmental Impact: Recycling prevents mercury release and recovers glass and aluminum.
light bulbs.Recycling Process: Machines crush the bulbs, capturing mercury vapor in filters while separating glass and metal.
light bulbs.Interesting Facts: Almost all components of a fluorescent bulb can be recycled.
light bulbs.Common Mistakes: Throwing LED or CFL bulbs into standard glass recycling bins.

metal waste.Preparation Steps: Rinse food cans and crush aluminum cans to save space.
metal waste.Disposal Warnings: Ensure aerosols are completely empty before recycling to prevent explosions.
metal waste.Environmental Impact: Recycling aluminum saves 95% of the energy needed to make new aluminum from bauxite ore.
metal waste.Recycling Process: Metals are shredded, melted in a furnace, cast into ingots, and rolled into new sheets.
metal waste.Interesting Facts: A recycled aluminum can is back on the grocery shelf in as little as 60 days.
metal waste.Common Mistakes: Leaving food heavily caked on the inside of tin cans.

organic waste.Preparation Steps: Remove all plastic stickers, rubber bands, or non-biodegradable packaging.
organic waste.Disposal Warnings: Avoid adding large amounts of meat or dairy to backyard compost to prevent pests.
organic waste.Environmental Impact: Composting prevents methane emissions from landfills and creates nutrient-rich soil.
organic waste.Recycling Process: Microorganisms break down the organic matter in an aerobic environment to create compost.
organic waste.Interesting Facts: Food waste makes up about 30% of what we throw away globally.
organic waste.Common Mistakes: Composting 'biodegradable' plastics in home setups (they often require industrial facilities).

paper waste.Preparation Steps: Keep dry and flatten cardboard boxes.
paper waste.Disposal Warnings: Do not recycle paper contaminated with food, grease, or bodily fluids.
paper waste.Environmental Impact: Recycling 1 ton of paper saves 17 trees and 7,000 gallons of water.
paper waste.Recycling Process: Paper is pulped in water, de-inked, screened for contaminants, and rolled into new sheets.
paper waste.Interesting Facts: Paper can be recycled 5 to 7 times before the fibers become too short.
paper waste.Common Mistakes: Trying to recycle greasy pizza boxes or wax-coated paper cups.

plastic waste.Preparation Steps: Rinse out food/liquid and check the resin identification code (triangle number).
plastic waste.Disposal Warnings: Soft plastics (like grocery bags) jam sorting machines and usually require special drop-offs.
plastic waste.Environmental Impact: Recycling plastic keeps it out of oceans and reduces petroleum consumption.
plastic waste.Recycling Process: Plastics are sorted by type, washed, shredded into flakes, melted, and extruded into pellets.
plastic waste.Interesting Facts: Recycled plastic bottles can be turned into fleece jackets or sleeping bag insulation.
plastic waste.Common Mistakes: Wish-cycling: throwing unrecyclable plastics (like styrofoam) into the bin hoping they get recycled.
